subject: Re: Redwood Private / VPC follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Redwood Private / VPC follow-up + next steps

Hi Samir / Laura —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key pain points you shared:
- Data residency requirement: PHI must remain in the US and be processed inside AcmeHealth VPC (no vendor-hosted storage).
- Air-gap / strict egress rules for clinical systems — limited outbound access and need for controlled jump boxes.
- Auditability: detailed request/response logs and KMS integration for key management.
- Throughput: expectation of 200 QPS for inference during peak hours; latency target ~100–150ms p95.

Goals for PoC:
1) Demonstrate Redwood Private deployed inside AcmeHealth VPC with VPC peering or PrivateLink.
2) Show end-to-end request flow from clinical app -> Redwood runtime with KV cache enabled.
3) Validate audit logs + KMS integration and measured latency under realistic load.

Constraints / notes:
- You mentioned procurement prefers a 6–8 week PoC window.
- Networking team will require a checklist for firewall rules, NACLs, and approved IP ranges.

Proposed next steps:
- I attached a networking checklist and our Private VPC overview (see attachments). Please share with your network/security team.
- Dev technical call: suggest Tue 2026-08-04 10:00–11:00 PT (Camila + Dev + your IT Ops) — confirm availability.
- Redwood security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence: I will send the initial package after you confirm the NDA.

Deliverables we’ll bring to the PoC:
- Deployment playbook for single-tenant Private (VPC peering or PrivateLink).
- Example IaC snippets for VPC/subnet/SGs and sample Helm charts.
- Load script for validating latency/throughput targets.

If that matches your understanding, we’ll lock the tech call and circulate the SOW draft for the PoC.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124
Redwood Inference

Camila — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 200 QPS is for anonymized triage workloads (no PHI at ingest) but responses may touch PHI in downstream processing — KMS + key rotation policies are critical.
- We need the networking checklist to include explicit egress rules and recommended NAT/Jumphost config for the air-gapped clusters.
- Procurement will require estimated PoC costs and an approximate recurring cost if we move to a dedicated deployment.

Availability: Tue 2026-08-04 10:00 PT works for our IT Ops (I’ll confirm with James).

Please loop in your security lead when you send the SOC2/controls package.

Thanks,
Samir

Hi Samir / James (IT Ops),

Attaching a concise networking checklist and an example security config for Private (see attached). Highlights below:
- Recommended: PrivateLink if you want zero public IPs; VPC peering if cross-account routing is simpler for your infra team.
- Required inbound rules: allow traffic on port 443 from your app subnets to the Redwood ingress ALB (we provide exact IP ranges).
- Recommended outbound: restrict to our provisioned NTP and KMS endpoints; if air-gap, consider an approved jump host for updates (we support offline package install).
- KMS: we support customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS/HSM) — we’ll provide key rotation guidelines and sample IAM policies.

Attached: AcmeHealth_Networking_Checklist.xlsx (worksheet: firewall_rules), Redwood_Private_VPC_Overview.pdf (section 3: deployment options).

Next steps from engineering:
1) Share your approved IP ranges and any proxy/jumpbox constraints before the tech call.
2) Confirm whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is preferred. We’ll prepare IaC templates accordingly.
3) We can do a dry run of the deployment in our lab and capture latency numbers to set expectations ahead of PoC.

Thanks — looking forward to the tech call.
Dev Patel
Platform Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
